tags.notes: Also known as Apuri or Anemone Valley. Clark's and tomato anemonefish confirmed by starfish.ch and malaysia-asia.my. Depth not stated by sources (one charter listing gives 3-25m); 20m is approximate. Re-audit 2026-11-27: earlier 'depth confirmed ~20m' claim and unfetchable sources (abyssoceanworld.com, thecrowdedplanet.com, merapitours.com) removed; other species unconfirmed by 2+ sources not listed.

Also known as Motolang. Swim-through depth reported 25m (starfish.ch) to 30m (alortanapi.com). Species at this site confirmed only by starfish.ch: Bargibant's and Pontohi seahorses, bluering octopus, two frogfish species, tawny nurseshark. Re-audit 2026-11-27: removed 14C cold-upwelling claim, bamboo sharks, marbled rays, leaffish, scorpionfish, visibility and best-season claims (no source found); nautikadivealor.com dropped (does not mention site). Max depth 35m unconfirmed.

Seamount/pinnacles between Kepa and Pura. Pinnacle tops at 7m and 2m (starfish.ch, which calls it Batu Kepa); other operators call it Batu Mandi. Species: starfish.ch list (barracuda, whitetip shark, marble ray, dogtooth tuna, Napoleon wrasse, trevally, sweetlips, coral crouchers, yellow-spotted scorpionfish); emperordivers.com and dive-the-world.com mention sharks/rays/barracuda. Re-audit 2026-11-27: removed ScubaBoard quote, giant/blue-fin trevally, hammerhead claim, Kal Muller naming claim and merapitours.com/underwaterasia.info/scubaboard.com (not re-fetched this session). Max depth 35m unconfirmed (one listing says ~40m).

No source confirms this specific site name. Closest match is 'Sharks Galore' (off eastern Pura Island) from starfish.ch and dive-the-world.com, but that source reported seeing no sharks and suggested renaming it. Could not obtain 3 independent confirmed sources. Wall type retained as plausible for Alor. Specific claims (silvertip sharks, groups 5-15) unverified. Re-audit 2026-07-10: fresh search repeated (starfish.ch full site list, dive-the-world.com, zubludiving.com via search) - 'Shark Close' still does not appear as a named site on any fetched primary source; one WebSearch synthesis claimed it appeared alongside invented-sounding site names ('Baruna's Point', 'Captain's Choice', 'The Refrigerator') with no source page confirming it, treated as an unreliable search-engine synthesis and disregarded. Remains unvalidated - do not pad with weak sources per policy. Re-audit 2026-11-27: still no source for the site name; markdown reduced to unconfirmed-site statement.

Slow drift over rugged boulder slope to ~25m (emperordivers.com); malaysia-asia.my calls it a healthy reef with mild-strong currents. Species: sea snakes (3 sources), lobsters (emperordivers.com, girlsthatscuba.com), lionfish (emperordivers.com), boxfish (girlsthatscuba.com). Re-audit 2026-11-27: site_type changed wall->reef (no source describes a wall); removed dolphins, Pura east-coast location, parrotfish/angelfish etc. list (merapitours.com not re-fetchable; 403).

Kalabahi Bay, also called Masjid Ampera. Steep black sand and rubble slope to 27m (dive-the-world.com). Species per starfish.ch, underwaterjournal.com (night dive: lacy and paddle-flap rhinopias, devilfish, painted frogfish, stargazer, crocodile snake eel, Spanish dancer), dan.org (blue-ringed and wonderpus octopus, bobtail squid). Re-audit 2026-11-27: 'steep slope to 90 feet' not found in the underwaterjournal article; depth now from dive-the-world.com.

Also known as Biatabang, Ternate Island (starfish.ch). Depth 28m (emperordivers.com, malaysia-asia.my) vs 30m (dive-the-world.com); overhangs at 30m (starfish.ch). Species: 6 nudibranch species (starfish.ch); orangutan crabs, squat lobsters, peacock mantis shrimp, morays, leaf scorpionfish (theoccasionaltraveller.com); sea snakes (girlsthatscuba.com); convict blennies (dan.org). Re-audit 2026-11-27: removed unsourced tidal-current reversal, visibility range, best-season and 'multiple sources rate introductory' claims.

Conflicting site descriptions found. starfish.ch (Tangaban, site 16) describes it as muck on a slope with pegasus sea moths and robust ghost pipefish. A second source describes 'Boardroom' as a wall on north Pura Island with 50m drop, caves, glassfish, jacks, snappers - possibly a different site with same name. Could not confirm 3 independent sources for either version. Wunderpus, mimic octopus, coconut octopus, flamboyant cuttlefish, seahorse species, frogfish species in existing markdown all unconfirmed. Re-audit 2026-07-10: re-fetched starfish.ch (verbatim entry #16 re-confirmed: 'two pegasus sea moths, a pair of robust ghostpipefishes and a large Kentrodoris rubescens nudibranch'). Searched again for a third independent source (Tangaban, nautikadivealor.com, alortanapi.com) - none list it. Remains at 2/needed-3 sources - stays unvalidated per policy rather than padding. Re-audit 2026-11-27: only starfish.ch lists it; markdown limited to its three confirmed species.

Pantar Strait is a geographic channel (site type drift is appropriate). Sources confirm very strong currents (documented 4-5 knots in description). Whale watching (blue whales, pilot whales, melon-headed whales, spinner dolphins Jun-Nov) confirmed. Hammerheads mentioned regionally but 'groups of 20-30' and 'silky sharks' are unconfirmed. Eagle rays, manta rays during migration also mentioned but not site-specific. The existing description overstates pelagic encounters. Could not verify 3 independent sources for the specific Pantar Strait as a dive site (vs. geographic area). Re-audit 2026-07-10: re-checked nautikadivealor.com and alortanapi.com - neither lists 'Pantar Strait' as a distinct named dive site (Munaseli, Bama, Halerman, etc. are the actual named sites within the strait). Re-confirmed via theoccasionaltraveller.com and ScubaBoard search that named sites within the strait (Bama Wall/'Great Wall of Pantar', Cathedral, Current Alley, Apuri/Clown Valley) are the actual dive stops; 'Pantar Strait' itself remains the geographic feature, consistent with prior finding. Remains unvalidated. Re-audit 2026-11-27: markdown limited to strong-current and boat-sighting facts (starfish.ch, theoccasionaltraveller.com).

Southern Pantar, black sand bay with volcanic hot springs (alortanapi.com). Three named sites in the bay (starfish.ch): Hot Property, Ribbon Eel Run, The Lava Flow; water generally colder. Species: alortanapi.com (ribbon eels, ghost pipefish, octopus, nudibranchs, hairy frogfish), dan.org (coconut octopus, bubble shells, juvenile lionfish), emperordivers.com (wonderpus). Re-audit 2026-11-27: bluewaterdivetravel.com not re-fetched, removed; depth 20m unconfirmed.

Names: Yellow Corner (alortanapi.com equates with Current Alley), Munaseli (theoccasionaltraveller.com, nautikadivealor.com). Depth ~20-30m depending on position (theoccasionaltraveller.com); 40m max unconfirmed. Species: hammerheads, blacktip sharks, barracuda, eagle rays, mobula rays, Napoleon wrasse, trevally; grey reef/silvertip sharks at Munaseli per nautikadivealor.com. Re-audit 2026-11-27: removed mola mola, 'scalloped' species claim and ewdr.com (not re-fetched); reef hook recommended rather than required.
